name: Healthcare CFO — Budget Variance & Comp Controls
narrative:
Dana Reyes is the CFO of a regional health system, and it's the Friday before the board meeting. The full-year operating-expense forecast is tracking about $4.1M over budget while recognized revenue is basically flat — so the board's question writes itself: is this a demand problem or a cost problem? Dana needs a board-ready answer, not a data project.

The dashboard tells the story in two pages: opex budget vs. actual vs. an AI_FORECAST to year-end, then a drill from the headline down through department, expense category, employed-vs-contractor, and vendor — landing on one line, Nursing contract labor (+$3.58M), where RN vacancies are backfilled with agency nurses at ~2x cost through a single staffing vendor. Ask Genie "why is Nursing over budget?" and it says the same thing in a sentence. Underneath, Unity Catalog enforces comp controls: Finance sees full compensation detail, Operations sees headcount only — same table, masked by policy.
